name: Cross-run reproducibility
definition: Evaluates whether three repeated live conversations under identical conditions preserve similar student behavior.
judge_context_inputs: three generated-student transcript sets (same task/persona/model, different repeats)

score_scales.1: Severe unreliability. Repeated runs imply different personas, incompatible knowledge levels, or contradictory emotional/behavioral profiles.
score_scales.2: Weak reproducibility. No Score 1 failure, but at least two runs materially differ in knowledge display, emotional tone, question pattern, or learning trajectory.
score_scales.3: Acceptable reproducibility. The same broad persona is recoverable across runs; topic order, wording, or depth may vary noticeably.
score_scales.4: Strong reproducibility. All runs preserve the same knowledge boundary, emotional profile, and question style with only natural variation.
score_scales.5: Excellent reproducibility. All runs show highly stable persona behavior across knowledge boundary, emotional tone, question pattern, and learning arc.

aggregation_formula: mean(overall_reproducibility), std(overall_reproducibility), high_score_ratio=count(overall_reproducibility >= 4)/n by model and tutor_temperature
